claims.text: Combining electromagnetic levitation with modulated differential scanning calorimetry will accurately and efficiently determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change at melting across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Containerless electromagnetic levitation eliminates container-induced contamination during melting.
High-speed optical pyrometry can monitor the temperature of the levitated HEA droplet.
Laser Doppler velocimetry can monitor the free-oscillation frequencies and damping of the levitated droplet.
The free oscillations of a levitated droplet depend on its surface tension, density, and shape.
Analysis of droplet oscillation frequency and damping can provide indirect measures of melting parameters and volume change.
Modulated DSC can provide direct calorimetric calibration of fusion heat flow.
A sinusoidal temperature perturbation in MDSC separates reversible heat-capacity changes from nonreversible fusion events.
MDSC thermal modulation can precisely resolve latent heat and expansion effects when thermal events overlap.
Cross-calibration of EML and MDSC measurements will refine extraction of fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
The method can operate over an approximate temperature range of 1000 °C to 2500 °C.
The combined method will determine melting temperatures and fusion properties with an uncertainty of approximately ±4–5%.
The combined method will reliably detect volume change at melting.
Liquid specific heat can be inferred from droplet oscillations and estimated within approximately ±4–5% when cross-validated against calorimetric data.
Liquid viscosity can be inferred from droplet oscillations and estimated within approximately ±4–5% when cross-validated against calorimetric data.
The approach is applicable to HEAs that form stable melts under containerless conditions and are feasible to measure by MDSC.
Severe baseline drift and non-spherical droplet behavior may reduce the method's applicability or accuracy.

The approach is ruled out if independently determined melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, or fusion entropy values from EML and MDSC disagree by more than 5% and cross-calibration cannot reconcile the discrepancy.
